patch:
diff --git a/evals/tasks/05-duplicate-orders/fixture/queries.py b/evals/tasks/05-duplicate-orders/fixture/queries.py
index 55fa844..732136e 100644
--- a/evals/tasks/05-duplicate-orders/fixture/queries.py
+++ b/evals/tasks/05-duplicate-orders/fixture/queries.py
@@ -1,11 +1,10 @@
-from store import CUSTOMERS, ORDERS
+from store import ORDERS
 
 
 def orders_for_customer(customer):
     """All orders belonging to `customer`."""
     rows = []
     for order in ORDERS:
-        owner = next(c for c in CUSTOMERS if c["id"] == order["customer_id"])
-        if owner["name"] == customer["name"]:
+        if order["customer_id"] == customer["id"]:
             rows.append(order)
     return rows
verification: 1) Before fix, run_tests.py -> 'visible tests passed' but build_report() showed 6 lines with 101/102 duplicated, total 290. 2) Applied fix (match by unique customer id). 3) After fix run_tests.py -> passed. 4) Report: 4 lines, total 165, distinct Zenith orders 103/104 both preserved. 5) git status --short shows only queries.py modified; git diff matches patch.
cause: Order attribution compared human-readable names; store contains two distinct customers named 'Acme', so every Acme order matched both, emitting each line once per matching customer and inflating total from 165 to 290. Matching on the order's customer_id makes lookup exact and unique.
